claim: Legislative authority of the Republic at the national level is vested in and exercised by Parliament.
No person or body other than Parliament may make law, except under authority given by the Constitution or by legislation.
The National Assembly represents the people of the constituencies and special interests, deliberates on issues of concern to the people, and enacts legislation.

The National Assembly determines the allocation of national revenue between the national and county levels, appropriates money for national government spending, and oversees national revenue and its spending.
The National Assembly reviews the conduct of the President, Deputy President and other State officers and starts the process of removing them; it oversees State organs.
The Senate represents the counties and protects the interests of the counties and their governments.
The Senate takes part in lawmaking by considering, debating and approving Bills concerning counties (Arts. 109 to 113).
The Senate determines the allocation of national revenue among counties (Art. 217) and oversees national revenue allocated to county governments.
The Senate considers and decides any resolution to remove the President or Deputy President (Art. 145).

The National Assembly has 290 members elected in constituencies, 47 women each elected by the voters of a county, 12 members nominated by parliamentary parties for special interests (youth, persons with disabilities, workers), and the Speaker.
The Senate has 47 members elected by county voters, 16 nominated women, 2 youth members, 2 members representing persons with disabilities (so 20 nominated in all), and the Speaker.
Parliament must work in the open, its sittings and its committees sit in public, and it must enable public participation in its business.
Every person has the right to petition Parliament on any matter within its authority, including to make, change or repeal a law.
Either House of Parliament and its committees can summon any person to give evidence or information, with the same powers as the High Court to enforce attendance and compel documents.

The President is Head of State and Government, exercises executive authority with the Deputy President and Cabinet Secretaries, is Commander-in-Chief of the Defence Forces and chairs the National Security Council.

The President nominates and, with National Assembly approval, appoints Cabinet Secretaries and other senior officers, chairs Cabinet and directs and co-ordinates ministries and government departments.
The Deputy President is the principal assistant of the President, deputises for the President, and performs the functions the Constitution gives and the President assigns.
A Cabinet Secretary must attend a committee of the National Assembly or the Senate when required and answer questions on matters for which the Cabinet Secretary is responsible.
National and county governments are distinct and interdependent and must work together by consultation and cooperation.
One object of devolution is to promote social and economic development and the provision of proximate, easily accessible services throughout Kenya.
Each county has a county government made up of a county assembly and a county executive.

A county assembly has members elected from wards (one per ward), special-seat members to meet the two-thirds gender rule, members of marginalised groups (including persons with disabilities and youth) and the Speaker; the elected and nominated members are chosen on the same day as a general election for MPs and serve five years (Art. 177(4)).

Executive authority of the county is exercised by the county executive committee: the governor, the deputy governor and members the governor appoints with assembly approval from outside the assembly. The governor and deputy are chief executive and deputy chief executive of the county.
The governor is elected by voters of the county on the same day as the general election; each candidate names a deputy who is elected with them; a person may serve at most two terms as governor.

A governor may be removed for gross violation of the Constitution or other law, serious reasons to believe a crime under national or international law was committed, abuse of office or gross misconduct, or physical or mental incapacity.
If the governor leaves office, the deputy governor takes over for the rest of the term.

The county executive committee implements county laws, implements national laws within the county where they require it, manages and coordinates the county administration and its departments, may draft proposed laws for the assembly, and must report regularly to the assembly.

Legislative authority of a county is vested in its county assembly, which may make laws needed to carry out Fourth Schedule functions and may oversee the county executive committee and other county executive organs.
A county assembly may receive and approve plans and policies for managing the county's resources and developing and managing its infrastructure and institutions.
A county assembly or its committees can summon any person to give evidence or information.
A county assembly must conduct business openly, sit in public, and enable public participation in its business and its committees.
The functions of the two levels are those in the Fourth Schedule; a function given to both is concurrent; a function not given to a county by the Constitution or national law is a national function.

A function can be transferred between levels by agreement if the receiving government can do it better and the money to do it moves too; constitutional responsibility stays with the level named in the Fourth Schedule.
Each level of government must respect the other's functional and institutional integrity and the two must cooperate, including through joint committees.
Police services (setting standards for recruitment, training and use of police; criminal law; correctional services) are national functions.
Courts are a national function.
Education policy, standards, curricula and examinations are national functions.
Universities and tertiary institutions, primary schools, special education, secondary schools and special education institutions are national functions.
Road traffic, the construction and operation of national trunk roads, and standards for the construction and maintenance of other roads by counties are national functions.
Housing policy and the general principles of land planning and co-ordination of planning by counties are national functions.
Protection of the environment and natural resources, including water protection, securing sufficient residual water, hydraulic engineering and dam safety, is a national function.
National referral health facilities and health policy are national functions.
Disaster management is listed as a national function.
Agricultural policy and veterinary policy are national functions.
Energy policy, including electricity and gas reticulation and energy regulation, is a national function.
County governments handle agriculture: crop and animal husbandry, livestock sale yards, county abattoirs, plant and animal disease control and fisheries.

County governments run county health services: county health facilities and pharmacies, ambulance services, primary health care, licensing food outlets, veterinary services, cemeteries and funeral parlours, and refuse removal, refuse dumps and solid waste disposal.
County governments control air pollution, noise pollution, other public nuisances and outdoor advertising.
County governments handle cultural activities, public entertainment and public amenities, including liquor licensing, libraries, sports facilities and county parks.
County transport is a county function: county roads, street lighting, traffic and parking, public road transport, and ferries and harbours (not regulation of international and national shipping).
Trade development and regulation is a county function: markets, trade licences (not regulation of professions), fair trading practices, local tourism and cooperative societies.
County planning and development is a county function: statistics, land survey and mapping, boundaries and fencing, housing, and electricity and gas reticulation and energy regulation.
Pre-primary education, village polytechnics, homecraft centres and childcare facilities are county functions.
Counties implement national policies on natural resources and environmental conservation, including soil and water conservation and forestry.
County public works and services are county functions, including storm water systems in built-up areas and water and sanitation services.
Fire fighting services and disaster management are listed as county functions.
Every child has the right to free and compulsory basic education.
Every person has the right to the highest attainable standard of health and to clean and safe water in adequate quantities.

Most public land is held by the county government in trust for county residents and administered for them by the National Land Commission; other public land is held by the national government and also administered by the Commission, which manages public land for both levels.
Judicial authority is exercised by the courts and tribunals set up under the Constitution.

The Inspector-General of Police has independent command of the National Police Service; the Cabinet Secretary may give policy direction but nobody may direct the Inspector-General on any particular investigation, enforcement against a person, or employment matter.
Public finance must be guided by openness, accountability and public participation in financial matters.

Every five years the Senate decides by resolution the basis for sharing among counties the revenue given to the county level, after taking advice from the Commission on Revenue Allocation, consulting governors and the Treasury Cabinet Secretary, and inviting public submissions.

Each year, at least two months before the financial year ends, a Division of Revenue Bill (national versus county share) and a County Allocation of Revenue Bill (share per county) must be brought to Parliament.
A county's share of national revenue must be transferred to it without undue delay and without deduction.
National law sets the structure of county development plans and budgets and when they are tabled in county assemblies.
The Treasury Cabinet Secretary submits national budget estimates to the National Assembly; a committee reviews them and takes public views; approved estimates go into an Appropriation Bill.
The Controller of Budget oversees implementation of national and county budgets by authorising withdrawals from public funds, and may not approve a withdrawal that is not authorised by law.

The county assembly vets and approves nominees to county public offices, approves the county budget and spending, approves borrowing and approves county development planning. (Text read: Revised edition as at 31 May 2019, hosted on leap.unep.org; later amendments not checked.)

A member of a county assembly must keep close contact with voters and consult them, present their views to the assembly, attend assembly and committee sessions, and link the assembly and the people on public service delivery. (2019 edition.)

A member of a county assembly shall not be directly or indirectly involved in the executive functions of the county government or in delivering services as if an officer or employee of the county government. (2019 edition.)

The governor executes the functions in the Constitution and legislation, represents the county, appoints the county executive committee with assembly approval, submits county plans and policies to the assembly, assents to bills passed by the assembly, chairs the executive committee, reports annually and gives a state of the county address. (2019 edition.)
The governor may dismiss a county executive committee member, and must do so if the county assembly resolves under s. 40. (2019 edition.)
The deputy governor deputises for the governor and may be given other portfolios by the governor. (2019 edition.)

To remove a governor: at least one-third of assembly members must back a motion, two-thirds must pass it, then the Senate hears the charges (it may appoint an 11-member committee) and the governor ceases to hold office only if a majority of all Senators vote to uphold a charge. (2019 edition.)

Each ward has a Ward Administrator, appointed competitively by the County Public Service Board, who coordinates, manages and supervises general administration in the ward, including service delivery and public participation. (2019 edition.)

Citizen participation in counties is based on access to information and to the process of making policies, laws and budgets; the county government must set up channels such as town hall meetings and budget preparation and validation forums. (2019 edition.)
No public money may be appropriated by a county outside a planning framework developed by the executive committee and approved by the county assembly. (2019 edition.)

Each county has a County Development Board chaired and convened by the Senator for the county, with the governor as vice-chair and the county's MPs, the Woman Representative, the deputy governor, assembly leaders and committee chairs, the County Secretary and the County Commissioner as members. It is a forum for consultation and gives input on county plans and annual budgets before they reach the assembly. (2019 edition. A 2015 High Court petition challenged s. 91A, [2015] KEHC 6965; we could not open the judgment and do not know the outcome.)
The county executive committee member for finance submits the budget estimates to the executive committee for approval, then to the county assembly. (2012 original text.)

The county assembly considers the county budget estimates and approves them with or without amendments so the appropriation law can pass by 30 June; a committee reviews them first and takes public views; amendments must follow the County Fiscal Strategy Paper and any increase must be balanced by a cut elsewhere. (2012 original text; later amendments not checked.)

The National Government Constituencies Development Fund is a national government fund of not less than 2.5% of the national government's share of revenue as divided in the annual Division of Revenue Act, administered by the NG-CDF Board. (NCLR Revised Edition 2023 as posted by NG-CDF.)
A project funded under the Act may only be for works and services within the exclusive functions of the national government. (Wording added by Act No. 21 of 2023.)

Each constituency has a Constituency Committee made up of a national government coordination official, three men, three women, one person with a disability, a Board officer and one co-opted member. The list of members in the 2023 revised text does not include the MP.
The Constituency Committee chair holds open ward forums, the Committee identifies priority projects and submits the list to the Board.
A Constituency Committee may, with Board approval, allocate funds to education bursary schemes, education days, teaching and learning activities and learner support programmes.
The National Assembly must set up a Select Committee on the NG-CDF (a chair and up to 18 other MPs) to oversee how the Act is carried out.
NG-CDF money must not be used to support political bodies or political activities or religious bodies or activities (a limited exception exists for emergency support in s. 25(4)).

The text before the 2026 appeal ruling tied the Fund Account Manager's custody of records to the term of Parliament; news reports say the Court of Appeal struck this subsection down on 6 February 2026.

The Supreme Court judgment struck down the earlier Constituencies Development Fund Act, 2013 for breaching separation of powers. (Case title and date confirmed from the Kenya Law listing; we could not open the judgment, outcome taken from news timelines.)
citation: Institute for Social Accountability & another v National Assembly & 5 others, Petition 1 of 2018, [2022] KESC 39 (KLR), 8 August 2022

claim: The High Court (Kimondo, Thande, Aburili JJ) declared the NG-CDF Act 2015, as amended in 2022 and 2023, unconstitutional, with two judges setting 30 June 2026 for the fund to stop. (Case title and date confirmed from the Kenya Law listing; orders taken from news reports because we could not open the judgment.)
citation: Gikonyo & another v National Assembly & 4 others, Constitutional Petition 178 of 2016, [2024] KEHC 10886 (KLR), 20 September 2024

claim: The Court of Appeal set aside the High Court judgment and upheld the NG-CDF Act except s. 43(9), which it found unconstitutional; the fund is operating under that ruling. (News reports only; judgment not opened.)
citation: Court of Appeal, consolidated Civil Appeal No. E884 of 2024, 6 February 2026 (as reported by TV47, 11 Aug 2026; Citizen Digital, Capital FM, Kahawatungu)

claim: The petitioners (Wanjiru Gikonyo and Cornelius Oduor Opuot) filed notice of their intention to challenge the Court of Appeal ruling at the Supreme Court. We found no Supreme Court merits judgment. A Supreme Court ruling on an application in the case ([2026] KESC 62, 25 September 2026) appeared in a search result but we could not read what it decided.
citation: Notice of intention to appeal to the Supreme Court, 6 February 2026 (Capital FM)

claim: The National Assembly passed a Bill on 1 July 2025 to put the NG-CDF (as the National Government Constituencies Fund), a Senate Oversight Fund and the NGAAF into the Constitution (new Arts. 204A to 204C). It still needed the Senate; we found no record of Senate action. Mzalendo lists the Bill as at Third Reading, updated 3 July 2026.
citation: National Assembly Bill No. 4 of 2025 (Constitution of Kenya (Amendment) Bill, 2025); Parliament news page 1 July 2025; https://www.mzalendo.com/legislative-trends/bills/na/514/

claim: The County Committee of the NGAAF has one person from each constituency in the county, a disability representative, the County Commissioner or nominee and national gender officers; it elects its own chair and vice-chair. The text we read does not list the Woman Representative as a member. (Treasury copy is marked "Revised" with blank gazette numbers; the gazetted version was not checked.)
citation: PFM (National Government Affirmative Action Fund) Regulations, 2016, reg. 16(2)-(5)

claim: Sources disagree on the legal base of the NGAAF (2015 or 2016 regulations under the PFM Act) and a 2026 parliamentary committee report recommends moving it into an Act of Parliament.
citation: NGAAF website, About page; 2026 Decentralized Funds Accounts Committee report (search result, not opened)

claim: Each county has a County Policing Authority chaired by the Governor or a county executive member the Governor appoints; it develops proposals on police priorities and targets for the county, and the Act does not let it interfere with any particular investigation or enforcement operation. (Revised edition 2014; later amendments not checked.)

A county government must establish water services providers, which are responsible for water services in their licensed area and for developing county water assets. (Original 2016 text; later amendments not checked.)

County governments provide the money for infrastructure for pre-primary education, childcare, homecraft centres and village polytechnics; the national government may transfer primary and secondary school infrastructure to a county by agreement under Art. 187. (2013 original text; the Act has since been amended, e.g. Act No. 3 of 2021.)

Counties do not yet have a fixed share of the road maintenance fuel levy. A Bill before Parliament would change that: the Senate roads committee proposed 49% and the Ministry about 15%. A June 2025 High Court ruling (Chemao v National Assembly) said counties should benefit and the Court of Appeal suspended it for 12 months. (News report only.)
citation: Roads Act (Amendment) Bill, 2025 (National Assembly Bill No. 34 of 2025) as reported by allAfrica, 11 May 2026

claim: The Kenya Roads Act 2007 created the Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA), Kenya Urban Roads Authority (KURA) and Kenya Rural Roads Authority (KeRRA); which agency looks after which road class depends on the road classification in the Act. We did not read the Act itself.
citation: Kenya Roads Act 2007 (Kenya Law page found by search; could not be opened by our tools)

claim: The detailed duties of an MP or Senator in the chamber and committees (questions, statements, committee membership, attendance rules) sit in the Standing Orders. We did not read them, so the guide leaves them out.
citation: Standing Orders of the National Assembly and of the Senate (not read)

claim: Some counties have county laws creating ward development funds. Their legality has been questioned: press reports say the Controller of Budget rejected Nairobi's fund twice. We did not find or read a court judgment or the Controller's decision, so treat this as contested and county by county.
citation: Ward development funds (news: Nation; Star, 15 Nov 2022)
